claims.text: The specific wear rate of HEA coatings on transition-metal matrices has a non-monotonic relationship with ambient temperature.
The initial improvement in tribological performance with increasing temperature is caused by strain-rate hardening.
The initial improvement in tribological performance with increasing temperature is caused by stabilization of an oxide film.
A transition from a protective tribo-oxide regime to a soft, plastic-flow-dominated regime causes sharp degradation at high temperature.
The tribolayer changes from a hard protective chromium/iron oxide scale to a soft, viscous, or delaminating oxide layer as temperature increases.
Elevated-temperature sliding causes dynamic recrystallization or phase instability in the HEA coating subsurface.
Between 25°C and 400°C, frictional heating promotes rapid formation of a dense, adherent oxide layer.
The dense, adherent oxide layer reduces the coefficient of friction.
The dense, adherent oxide layer acts as a barrier against abrasive wear.
Above the critical temperature, the oxide layer loses structural integrity through viscous behavior or spalling.
Above the critical temperature, thermal softening substantially reduces the yield strength of the HEA coating.
Oxide-layer failure and coating softening lead to severe adhesive wear and material transfer.
High configurational entropy delays thermal softening relative to conventional alloys.
The specific wear rate decreases by a factor of 2–5 as temperature increases from 25°C to approximately 400°C.
The specific wear rate reaches a minimum at approximately 400°C.
Above approximately 400°C, the specific wear rate increases exponentially.
Severe adhesive-wear failure occurs after the predicted degradation boundary is exceeded.
The performance-degradation boundary occurs at 550°C ± 50°C.
At the degradation boundary, rapid diffusion-controlled oxidation forms non-protective porous oxides.
At the degradation boundary, the HEA yield strength falls below the stress required to maintain a stable tribolayer.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome places the wear-rate minimum and onset of exponential degradation at about 400°C, while the stated performance-degradation boundary is 550°C ± 50°C. The distinction between an onset near 400°C and a degradation boundary at 500–600°C is not defined, creating an internally inconsistent critical-temperature specification.
